texts.facts: The petitioners have filed these petitions U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the SCCH17 3 MVC No. 6204 & 6205/2018 injuries sustained by them, in a road traffic accident that occurred on 08.10.2018. 2. The petition averments in brief are as under: On 08.10.2018 at about 11.05 a.m., the petitioner in MVC No. 62042018 was riding the two wheeler bearing Reg. No. KA51ER0345 along with his mother i.e., the petitioner in MVC 62052018, near Anjanapura lake, nice road, Bengaluru, at that time the driver of the car bearing Reg. No. KA04MJ2767 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner with high speed suddenly applied break without giving any indication in the middle of the road, due to which the petitioners who were from coming behind the car dashed to the car. Due to the impact, both the petitioners fell down and sustained grievous injuries. Immediately after the accident, both petitioners In Mvc 6204/2018: Supreeth H.N vs Shivaswamy H.K on 2 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27625777/ 2 were shifted to Sri Sai Ram Hospital, later the petitioner SCCH17 4 MVC No. 6204 & 6205/2018 in MVC No.62052018 was shifted to Fortis Hospital, wherein she was admitted as an inpatient. The petitioner in MVC 6204/2018 spent Rs.1,00,000/ towards medical expenses and the petitioner in MVC 6205/2018 has spent Rs.3,00,000/ towards medical expenses. The petitioner in MVC 596/2020 was working in a private company and earning Rs.25,000/ p.m., The petitioner in MVC 597/2020 was doing tailoring work and earning Rs.15,000/ p.m. Due to the accidental injuries, the petitioners are not able to continue their work and under complete bed rest and they were suffering from permanent disability. The respondent No.1 and 2 are the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle. Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners. Hence the petitioners prays to award SCCH17 5 MVC No. 6204 & 6205/2018 compensation of Rs.15,00,000/ each with interest, respectively. 3. After service of notices both the respondents appeared. But respondent No.1 has not chosen to file written statement. Respondent No.2 appeared through its advocate and filed objection statement admitting issuance of insurance policy to the car bearing Reg. No. KA04MJ 2767 and the liability, of this respondent, if any, is In Mvc 6204/2018: Supreeth H.N vs Shivaswamy H.K on 2 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27625777/ 3 subject to terms and conditions of the policy and the driver of the said vehicle was not having valid driving licence as on the date of accident. Further contended that the accident was occurred due to the negligence on the part of rider of the motor cycle i.e., the petitioner in MVC 62042018. There is no negligence on the part of driver of the car. Further denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioners. The compensation as claimed by the petitioners are highly excessive and exorbitant. SCCH17 6 MVC No. 6204 & 6205/2018 Accordingly, respondent No.2 prays to dismiss the petition against it. 4. On the basis of rival contention, the following issues have been framed in both the petitions : ISSUES IN MVC No. 6204/2018 1. along with her son near Anjananapura lake, Nice Road, Bangalore met with an accident and sustained injuries due to negligence on the part of driver of car bearing Reg. No. KA04MJ2767 as alleged? 5 . The petitioners, to prove their case got examined themselves as PW.1 and 2, the documents are marked at Ex.P1 to 18. Consequently, the petitioner Supreeth H.N. who was riding the motor cycle hit the car from the back side. After receipt of notice, first respondent issued reply stating that he is the RC owner of the said car and one Vishal was driving the said car as on the date of accident. Due to which, the petitioner in MVC In Mvc 6204/2018: Supreeth H.N vs Shivaswamy H.K on 2 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27625777/ 7 No.62042018 who was riding the motor cycle along with his mother i.e., the petitioner in MVC 62052018 fell down from the bike and sustained grievous injuries. Hence, police have lead charge sheet against the accused. 12. One Krishnappa V. who is working as Medical Records Officer at Sri. Sai Ram Hospital is examined as PW.3. PW.5 deposed that, he examined the petitioner and stated that the petitioner sustained left distal radius fracture and he underwent closed reduction and internal fixation with K wire on 8.10.2018. Xray shows united distal radius fracture. The petitioner suffers disability of left arm at 32% and whole disability at 11%. The petitioner has produced medical bills as per Ex.P17 for Rs.2,29,844/.
texts.arguments: In the written statement the second respondent has taken up a main defence that the alleged accident occurred solely due to negligence of the rider of the motor cycle i.e., petitioner in MVC 62042018 that means second respondent also do not dispute the accident. 16 . During the course of argument, the learned counsel for second respondent has relied on the following decisions reported in; 2008 ACJ 1188 between Renukadevi H. V/s. Bangalore Metropolitan Transport Corporation and another, 2009 ACJ 2003 between Raj Rani and others V/s. Oriental Ins. Co. Ltd., and others, ILR 2010 KAR 2439 between Sri. Subash V/s. The In Mvc 6204/2018: The petitioner has also produced 9 medical bills which are marked at Ex.P.14, amounting to Rs.75,558/. 25. The petitioner has produced vehicle repair bill as per Ex.P18 for Rs.45,651/. But he has not produced RC card to show his ownership over the vehicle.
